startup.context: Identified a Flask/Connexion API (app.py) with existing Dockerfile and docker-compose.yaml. Started the existing Compose project, which launches secure and vulnerable app instances. Verified the target app is serving from the vulnerable instance with HTTP 200 at GET / on http://127.0.0.1:5002/; the secure instance on 5001 also returned 200.

scanPrep.context:
Summary: Prepared the app for DAST by extending JWT lifetime for the scanned service and verifying the real login endpoint accepts rapid repeated authentication requests without throttling; no server-side rate limiting, lockout, or CAPTCHA controls were present in this Flask/Connexion app.
Change: Added `tokentimetolive=999999` to the `vampi-vulnerable` service in `docker-compose.yaml` so JWT auth sessions last long enough for DAST scanning.
Change: Rebuilt/recreated only the `vampi-vulnerable` service with `docker compose up -d --build vampi-vulnerable`, then re-seeded the app via `GET /createdb` because the SQLite DB is recreated with the container.
Change: Verified the live app by sending 6 rapid `POST http://localhost:5002/users/v1/login` requests using seeded credentials (`name1` / `pass1`); all returned HTTP 200 success with no 429, throttle, lockout, or challenge responses.
Change: Inspected runtime env/config, installed packages, and source for Flask/Connexion security controls; found no server-side rate limiter, account lockout, CAPTCHA, or CSRF enforcement to relax.
Recovery guidance (security controls): For future scan prep on this repo, use the same targeted rebuild path: `docker compose up -d --build vampi-vulnerable`. After recreate, initialize the DB with `GET http://localhost:5002/createdb` before auth tests. Verify scanner readiness against the real auth path with repeated `POST /users/v1/login` requests using seeded creds `name1` / `pass1`, and confirm responses stay HTTP 200 without bodies mentioning rate limits/throttling. The long-lived auth setting is persisted in `docker-compose.yaml` as `tokentimetolive=999999`.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): No 2FA bypass is needed for this app. Relevant findings: code search for twoFactor/2fa/mfa/totp/otp/authenticator/verification returned no matches; the users table only has id, username, password, email, and admin columns; after GET http://localhost:5002/createdb, logging in with admin/pass1 at POST /users/v1/login returns a JWT and GET /me with Bearer auth returns 200 with the admin profile. If rechecking later, you can verify with: docker compose ps, curl http://localhost:5002/createdb, then POST /users/v1/login and GET /me with the returned token.
